title: Cap. IX: Melchizedek over Levi; mediate propagation close — before Caput X
pass_a_gloss: What, then, is Paul's actual reasoning? His aim is to prove Levitical priestly dignity lower than Melchizedek's. The lever is Abraham's paying tithes to Melchizedek. Paul compares Levi and Melchizedek in their priestly office; 'Levi' covers the Levitical priests and their whole priesthood. Both sides received tithes, so far equal. Then four differences lift Melchizedek far above: (1) Levites had a command to take tithes; Melchizedek has none on record; (2) Levites took tithes from brothers sprung from Abraham's loins — equals by nature — while Melchizedek, not of that stock, took tithes from their father Abraham who held the promises, so Levites inherited priesthood from Abraham and Melchizedek had his from elsewhere; Levites' blessings to brothers came from Abraham, but Abraham received blessing from Melchizedek; (3) Levites take tithes as death-liable men who need them; Melchizedek as one Scripture marks as living on / immortal, so tithes declare dignity; (4) Levi who takes tithes can himself be said, through tithed Abraham, to have been tithed by Melchizedek — still in the father's loins when Melchizedek met Abraham, before Isaac, by God's singular providence so the Levitical dignity would not seem already split off. God chose the moment when undivided flesh-posterity dignity still sat in one Abraham, later split so Levi got priestly and Judah royal inheritance. Cast as a syllogism: whoever was tithed by that providence while still holding the whole Levitical dignity untseparated — in him the Levitical priesthood / Levite priests were, so to speak, tithed; Abraham was so tithed; therefore the Levite priests were, so to speak, tithed. That was the homage the contained Levitical priesthood paid Melchizedek through Abraham. Levi's priesthood was only what he received by hereditary right from Abraham under God's assigning and forming. Kind reader: Paul's reason stands invincible, and his wording yields no imputation properly so called unless perhaps a mediate one. As Levitical priesthood was in Abraham and derived to Levi, so sin was in Adam and propagated to us. Same dignity-judgment for Levi/Abraham priests; same guilt-judgment for Adam and for us under the inherent vice drawn from him. Feudal homage paid by a father while the son still hid in the loins would make the son a vassal without imputing the father's homage to the son — else the son could not be asked to pay it again.
pass_b_english: You will ask, then: what is the Apostle's reasoning? The aim is to prove that the dignity of the Levitical priesthood is less than Melchizedek's. He draws the argument from this: that tithes were paid by Abraham to Melchizedek. To explain that and bring it into the light, he sets a comparison between Levi and Melchizedek with an eye to their priestly office. By the name Levi he takes in the Levitical priests and their whole priesthood. If Melchizedek received tithes, the Levitical priests also used to receive tithes. So far, then, they were equals in a way. But the Apostle notes four differences that raise Melchizedek immensely above the Levitical priests. First: to these a command had been given to receive tithes, while of him no such command stands. Second: these received tithes from their brothers, come out of Abraham's loins and therefore equal to them by nature and origin; but he, not being of the same stock, received tithes not from the Levites' brothers, but from their father himself — Abraham, who had the promises. So these received their priesthood and dignity from Abraham as his heirs; he had his from elsewhere. These drew every blessing they gave their brothers from Abraham who had the promises; but he did not receive blessing from Abraham — on the contrary, Abraham received it from him, though Abraham had the promises. Third: these receive tithes as men liable to death, and therefore needing them; but he as one whom Scripture testifies lives continually, or is immortal — so that tithes could not be given him except to declare his dignity. Fourth: even Levi himself, who received tithes, can be said in a way to have been tithed by Melchizedek through Abraham who was tithed. For he was still in his father's loins when Melchizedek met Abraham. This happened before Isaac was begotten. Without doubt that came about not by chance but by God's singular providence, lest, once Levi was separated from him, the dignity of the Levitical priesthood should seem already separated from him then. So God chose that time when, in one Abraham, with no separation of heirs yet made from him, the whole dignity of his posterity according to the flesh was contained as one — which in its time was so distributed among his sons that Levi became heir of the priestly dignity, Judah of the royal. If anyone demands that I cast the Apostle's reason in syllogistic form, it can be framed thus: Whoever by God's singular providence was then tithed when he still contained in himself the whole dignity of the Levitical priesthood, no separation yet made from him — in him, being tithed, the Levitical priesthood itself, or the Levite priests, so to speak, were tithed. But by God's singular providence Abraham was then tithed when he still contained in himself the whole dignity of the Levitical priesthood, no separation yet made from him. Therefore in him, being tithed, the Levite priests, so to speak, were tithed. For this, so to speak, was the homage the Levitical priesthood paid Melchizedek through Abraham, in whom it was contained. For Levi had no other priesthood than what, received from Abraham by hereditary right, God assigning and forming it, was inducted into him. Hence, kind reader, I think you see clearly both that the Apostle's reason is invincible, and that in his words there is no imputation properly so called — unless perhaps a mediate one. For as in Abraham was the Levitical priesthood, and from him it was derived to Levi, so in Adam was sin, and from him it has been propagated to us. Therefore as the same judgment was to be made of Levi the priest and of Abraham the priest as to the dignity of the priesthood, so the same judgment is to be made, as to guilt, of Adam the sinner and of us sinners on account of the inherent vice drawn from him. If someone were said, while still hiding in his father's loins, so to speak, to have paid the lord of a fief the homage they call homage, and so to be that lord's vassal, as they speak: would the argument not proceed rightly? And yet the homage paid by the father would not be imputed to the son: for if it were, it could no more be required of the son that he pay it again himself than it could be required of the parent.
source_text: Quaeram igitur, inquies, est Apostoli ratiocinatio? Scopus est probare Sacerdotii Levitici quam Melchisedecici dignitatem esse minorem. Argumentum ex eo ducit, quod Melchisedeco decimae sunt ab Abrahamo solutae. Quod ut explicet, atque proferat in lucem, comparationem instituit inter Levi & Melchisedecum habita ratione muneris ipsorum Sacerdotalis. Levi autem nomine Sacerdotes Leviticos, totumque eorum sacerdotium complectitur. Si Melchisedecus decimas accepit, etiam ipsi sacerdotes Levitici decimas accipiebant. Hactenus igitur quodammodo pares erant. Sed quatuor observat Apostolus differentias Melchisedecum supra Sacerdotes Leviticos, immane quantum, extollentes. Prima est, quod his datum erat mandatum accipiendi decimas, cum de illo nullum extet ejusmodi mandatum. Altera, quod hi decimas accipiebant a fratribus suis, egressis e lumbis Abrahae, ac proinde natura & origine sibi aequalibus; Ille vero, cum non esset ex eodem genere, decimas accepit, non a Levitarum fratribus, sed ab ipso eorum patre, Abrahamo, habente promissiones. Itaque hi ab Abrahamo sacerdotium ac dignitatem suam tanquam illius haeredes acceperunt; Ille suam aliunde habuit. Hi suam omnem benedictionem quam fratribus impertierunt ab Abrahamo habente promissiones traxerunt; Ille vero benedictionem non accepit ab Abrahamo, sed contra Abrahamus ab ipso, cum tamen hic promissiones haberet. Tertia, quod hi accipiant decimas tanquam homines morti obnoxii, ac proinde eis egentes; Ille vero tanquam is, quem perpetuo vivere, seu immortalem esse Scriptura testatur: ut non potuerint ei decimae dari, nisi declarandae ejus dignitatis gratia. Quarta denique quod etiam ipse Levi, qui decimas accepit, per Abrahamum decimatum quodammodo decimatus fuisse a Melchisedeco dici possit. Nam is adhuc erat in lumbis patris, cum Abrahamo occurreret Melchisedecus. Hoc enim evenit antequam Isaacus esset genitus. Id quod non casu, sed singulari Dei providentia sine dubio accidit, ne separato ab eo Levi, videretur etiam ab eo tunc separata fuisse Levitici sacerdotii dignitas. Itaque id tempus elegit Deus, cum in uno Abrahamo nondum ulla ab eo facta haeredum separatione, omnis posteritatis ejus secundum carnem unita contineretur dignitas, quae suo tandem tempore inter ejus filios ita est distributa, ut sacerdotalis dignitatis Levi, regiae Juda haeres fieret. Quod si quis a me flagitet, ut rationem Apostoli Syllogismi forma induam: is sic poterit concipi. Qui singulari Dei providentia tunc est decimatus, cum adhuc in se sacerdotii Levitici dignitatem, nondum ulla facta ab eo separatione, totam contineret, in eo decimato ipsum sacerdotium Leviticum, seu ipsi Levitae sacerdotes, ut ita loquar, decimati fuerunt. Atqui singulari Dei providentia tunc est decimatus Abrahamus, cum adhuc in se Sacerdotii Levitici dignitatem, nondum ulla facta ab eo separatione, totam contineret. Ergo in eo decimato Levitae sacerdotes, ut ita loquar, decimati fuerunt. Hoc enim, ut ita dicam, homagium Sacerdotium Leviticum per Abrahamum, in quo continebatur, Melchisedeco exhibuit. Non enim aliud habuit Levi sacerdotium, quam quod ab Abrahamo haereditario jure acceptum, Deo attribuente & formante, ipsi inductum fuit. Hinc, opinor, Lector benevole perspicis, cum invictam esse rationem Apostoli, tum in ejus verbis nullam proprie dictam imputationem haberi, nisi forte mediatam. Nam ut in Abrahamo fuit Sacerdotium Leviticum, ex eoque ad Levi est derivatum, sic in Adamo fuit peccatum, ex eoque in nos est propagatum. Itaque ut idem de Levi sacerdote ac de Abrahamo sacerdote faciendum, quantum ad dignitatem sacerdotii spectat, judicium fuit, sic de Adamo peccatore & nobis ob tractum ab eo inhaerens vitium peccatoribus, idem, quoad reatum, faciendum judicium est. Si diceretur aliquis Domino feudi in suo patre, cum in ejus lumbis adhuc delitesceret, ut ita loquar, homagium quod vocant praestitisse, itaque Domini illius, ut loquuntur, vassallum esse: nonne recte procederet argumentum? Et tamen non imputaretur praestitum a patre homagium filio: nam si imputaretur, non magis a filio exigi posset ut id ipse denuo praestaret, quam id poterat a parente exigi.
